MATHEMATICS — TERMLY EXAM #4 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is the 6th multiple of 4? (1 mark)
   A. 24
   B. 20
   C. 10
   D. 28

2. What is the next number in the pattern 2, 8, 14, 20, ...? (1 mark)
   A. 26
   B. 27
   C. 32
   D. 25

3. In the number 4,835, the digit 3 is in which place? (1 mark)
   A. Hundreds
   B. Tens
   C. Thousands
   D. Ones

4. A library has 5,208 story books and 3,796 textbooks. How many books does it have? (1 mark)
   A. 10,004 books
   B. 9,104 books
   C. 9,004 books
   D. 8,994 books

5. Work out 3,999 + 4,001. (1 mark)
   A. 7,900
   B. 8,000
   C. 8,010
   D. 7,990

6. A farmer picked 1,275 mangoes on Monday and 3,548 mangoes on Tuesday. How many mangoes did he pick? (1 mark)
   A. 4,713 mangoes
   B. 4,923 mangoes
   C. 4,823 mangoes
   D. 4,813 mangoes

7. Estimate 7,483 − 2,196 by rounding each number to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 5,380
   B. 5,270
   C. 5,280
   D. 5,290

8. Work out 4,000 − 1,236. (1 mark)
   A. 2,664
   B. 3,236
   C. 2,764
   D. 2,774

9. What is 24 × 30? (1 mark)
   A. 54
   B. 720
   C. 7,200
   D. 72

10. Work out 43 × 12. (1 mark)
   A. 506
   B. 516
   C. 526
   D. 129

11. What is 60 × 100? (1 mark)
   A. 160
   B. 6,000
   C. 600
   D. 60,000

12. What is 91 ÷ 7? (1 mark)
   A. 23
   B. 14
   C. 12
   D. 13

13. What is 58 ÷ 4? (1 mark)
   A. 15 remainder 2
   B. 14 remainder 2
   C. 14 remainder 3
   D. 13 remainder 6

14. What is 47 ÷ 5? (1 mark)
   A. 9 remainder 3
   B. 8 remainder 7
   C. 10 remainder 2
   D. 9 remainder 2

15. In the fraction 4/12, which number is the denominator? (1 mark)
   A. 12
   B. 8
   C. 4
   D. 16

16. In the fraction 2/9, which number is the denominator? (1 mark)
   A. 7
   B. 11
   C. 9
   D. 2

17. Change 3 3/4 to an improper fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 16/4
   B. 15/4
   C. 6/4
   D. 12/4

18. Which is the largest number: 0.7, 0.07, 0.75, 0.57? (1 mark)
   A. 0.7
   B. 0.57
   C. 0.75
   D. 0.07

19. Which is the smallest number: 1.2, 1.02, 1.25, 1.052? (1 mark)
   A. 1.02
   B. 1.2
   C. 1.052
   D. 1.25

20. What is the total value of the digit 4 in 13.42? (1 mark)
   A. 0.4
   B. 4
   C. 0.04
   D. 400

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Change 45/100, 6/100 and 7/10 into decimals. (3 marks)

22. Write 0.7, 0.07, 0.75 and 0.57 in order from the smallest to the largest. (3 marks)

23. 38 mangoes are shared equally among 5 children. How many does each child get and how many are left over? (3 marks)

24. Divide 96 by 3 by dividing the tens first and then the ones. (3 marks)

25. Write 0.8 and 0.37 as fractions. (2 marks)

26. Write the first five multiples of 9. (2 marks)

27. Write the next three numbers in the pattern 2,000, 2,300, 2,600, 2,900. (3 marks)

28. Add 6,478 and 2,355 and check by estimating to the nearest ten. (4 marks)

29. Arrange these prices from the cheapest to the most expensive: Ksh 8.25, Ksh 8.05, Ksh 8.50, Ksh 7.99. (3 marks)

30. Estimate 5,382 + 3,617 by rounding each number to the nearest ten. Then find the exact sum. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — TERMLY EXAM #4 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — 24
   Multiply 4 × 6 = 24. It is the 6th multiple of 4.

2. A — 26
   The rule is add 6. 20 + 6 = 26.

3. B — Tens
   Counting from the right the places are ones, tens, hundreds, thousands and ten thousands. The digit 3 is in the tens place.

4. C — 9,004 books
   Add 5,208 + 3,796 = 9,004 books.

5. B — 8,000
   Add ones, tens, hundreds and thousands, regrouping when a column is 10 or more. 3,999 + 4,001 = 8,000.

6. C — 4,823 mangoes
   Add 1,275 + 3,548 = 4,823 mangoes.

7. C — 5,280
   7,483 rounds to 7,480 and 2,196 rounds to 2,200. 7,480 − 2,200 = 5,280.

8. C — 2,764
   Subtract from the ones, regrouping when the top digit is smaller. 4,000 − 1,236 = 2,764. Check: 2,764 + 1,236 = 4,000.

9. B — 720
   24 × 3 = 72, then × 10 gives 720.

10. B — 516
   43 × 2 = 86 and 43 × 10 = 430. 86 + 430 = 516.

11. B — 6,000
   Multiplying by 100 moves each digit two places to the left, so 60 × 100 = 6,000.

12. D — 13
   7 × 13 = 91, so 91 ÷ 7 = 13.

13. B — 14 remainder 2
   4 × 14 = 56 and 58 − 56 = 2. So 58 ÷ 4 = 14 remainder 2. Check: 14 × 4 + 2 = 58.

14. D — 9 remainder 2
   5 × 9 = 45 and 47 − 45 = 2. So 47 ÷ 5 = 9 remainder 2. Check: 9 × 5 + 2 = 47.

15. A — 12
   The denominator is the bottom number. It shows how many equal parts the whole is cut into.

16. C — 9
   The denominator is the bottom number. It shows how many equal parts the whole is cut into.

17. B — 15/4
   3 × 4 = 12 and 12 + 3 = 15. The denominator stays 4, so the answer is 15/4.

18. C — 0.75
   Give every number the same number of decimal places and compare from the left. The largest number is 0.75.

19. A — 1.02
   Give every number the same number of decimal places and compare from the left. The smallest number is 1.02.

20. A — 0.4
   The digit 4 is in the tenths place, so its total value is 0.4.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: 0.45, 0.06 and 0.7
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct decimal.

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: 0.07, 0.57, 0.7, 0.75
   Working / marking points: Write with two decimal places: 0.70, 0.07, 0.75, 0.57. 1 mark for 0.07 first, 2 marks for the rest in order.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: Each child gets 7 mangoes and 3 mangoes are left over.
   Working / marking points: 38 ÷ 5 = 7 remainder 3. 1 mark for the division, 1 mark for 7, 1 mark for 3.

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: 32
   Working / marking points: 9 tens ÷ 3 = 3 tens (1 mark); 6 ones ÷ 3 = 2 ones (1 mark); answer 32 (1 mark).

25. (2 marks)
   Answer: 8/10 and 37/100
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct fraction.

26. (2 marks)
   Answer: 9, 18, 27, 36, 45
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the first three and 1 mark for the last two.

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: 3,200, 3,500, 3,800 (rule: add 300)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the rule and 2 marks for the three correct numbers.

28. (4 marks)
   Answer: Exact 8,833. Estimate 6,480 + 2,360 = 8,840, which is close.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for the exact sum with regrouping, 1 mark for rounding both numbers, 1 mark for the estimate.

29. (3 marks)
   Answer: Ksh 7.99, Ksh 8.05, Ksh 8.25, Ksh 8.50
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 7.99 first and 2 marks for the correct order of the rest.

30. (4 marks)
   Answer: Estimate: 5,380 + 3,620 = 9,000. Exact: 8,999.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rounded number, 1 mark for the estimate 9,000, 1 mark for the exact sum 8,999.
